chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the woman who performs khal' (redemption/divorce by wife's initiative). He said: 'It is not permissible for her husband to divorce her (accept the khal') until she says: "I will not be dutiful to you with an oath, and I will not establish God's boundaries within you, and I will not perform the ritual bath for you from major impurity, and I will surely make your bed fertile (bear children for you), and I will surely bring into your house someone you dislike without your knowledge." And they (the husband and witnesses) do not speak, so she is the one who says this. When she performs khal', she is divorced (bain), and he is entitled to take from her wealth whatever he can, but he is not entitled to take from the mukhalli'ah (the woman) all that he gave her.'

key_terms.الْمُبَارَأَةِ: The woman who performs the separation/khal'
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةِ: The woman who initiates khal' (divorce by her own choice/financial redemption)
key_terms.بَائِنٌ: Divorced (specifically referring to bain, a revocable or irrevocable separation depending on context, here implying the marriage is dissolved)
key_terms.يَخْلَعَ: To divorce or release (specifically in the context of khal')

ai.seo_question: What are the specific verbal conditions required for a valid khal' divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific verbal formula required for *khal'* (wife-initiated divorce), emphasizing that the wife must explicitly declare her future disobedience (*nushuz*) to validate the transaction. It clarifies the financial implications, noting that while the husband may reclaim assets he gave her, he is not entitled to the entire *mubar'ah* (compensation) amount, reflecting the Shia juristic view on equitable settlement. This narration underscores the procedural rigor in Shia fiqh to prevent arbitrary divorce by ensuring clear intent and specific declarations from the wife.
